record.original_question: Can phase-retrieval reconstructions be justified by attaching statistically meaningful confidence intervals, including possibly pixel-wise confidence intervals, to the recovered object?

evidence.quote: 4. Can we justify the obtained reconstruction by providing (pixel-wise) confidence intervals?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the phase retrieval problem: given measurements $y = |\mathcal{A} x^\star|^2 + \eta$, where $x^\star \in \mathbb{C}^n$ (or $\mathbb{R}^n$) is an unknown object (e.g. an image arranged on a pixel grid), $\mathcal{A}: \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{C}^m$ is a known linear measurement operator (such as an oversampled Fourier transform, coded-diffraction operator, or ptychographic operator), $|\cdot|^2$ is taken componentwise, and $\eta$ is a noise vector drawn from a known statistical model (e.g. additive Gaussian or Poisson). Suppose a reconstruction algorithm produces an estimator $\hat x = \hat x(y)$ of $x^\star$.

Develop a methodology that, for any prescribed confidence level $1-\alpha \in (0,1)$, attaches to the reconstruction $\hat x$ statistically meaningful confidence intervals — in particular, pixel-wise confidence intervals $[L_i(y), U_i(y)]$ for each coordinate (or pixel) $i \in \{1,\dots,n\}$ of $x^\star$ (or for the magnitude $|x^\star_i|$ and phase $\arg x^\star_i$ separately) — such that
$$\Pr\bigl(x^\star_i \in [L_i(y), U_i(y)] \text{ for all } i \in S \bigr) \ge 1-\alpha,$$
for an appropriate (joint, marginal, or false-coverage-controlled) coverage criterion, while accounting for the inherent global phase / sign / translation ambiguities of phase retrieval. Establish rigorous guarantees on the validity (coverage) and informativeness (width) of such intervals under realistic noise models, and thereby justify phase-retrieval reconstructions through quantitative uncertainty quantification.
artifact.status_search_result: Several recent works propose pixel-wise uncertainty quantification for imaging inverse problems and specifically for phase retrieval: Bayesian neural network approaches yield per-pixel uncertainty maps for deep-learning phase imaging; conformal prediction and conformalized quantile regression provide distribution-free pixel-wise intervals with finite-sample coverage guarantees; and debiased-estimator approaches construct Gaussian confidence regions for complex pixel values from which magnitude and phase intervals follow. While useful methodologies exist, a fully general, statistically rigorous theory of pixel-wise confidence intervals for phase retrieval (handling intrinsic ambiguities and nonconvexity uniformly) remains an active research direction rather than a settled question.

status_evidence.title: Reliable deep-learning-based phase imaging with uncertainty quantification
status_evidence.snippet: BNN-predicted uncertainty maps provide a per-pixel estimate of the confidence level of the deep learning prediction in phase imaging.
status_evidence.claim: Pixel-wise uncertainty maps for phase retrieval have been constructed via Bayesian neural networks.

status_evidence.title: Image-to-Image Regression with Distribution-Free Uncertainty Quantification
status_evidence.snippet: Methods derive uncertainty intervals around each pixel guaranteed to contain the true value with user-specified confidence, with formal guarantees regardless of model.
status_evidence.claim: Distribution-free pixel-wise confidence intervals with coverage guarantees can be obtained for image reconstruction.

status_evidence.title: Task-Driven Uncertainty Quantification in Inverse Problems via Conformal Prediction
status_evidence.snippet: A statistically rigorous framework based on conformalized quantile regression as an add-on to any image reconstruction method to yield spatially resolved uncertainty intervals.
status_evidence.claim: Conformal prediction provides valid pixel-level uncertainty intervals for inverse-problem reconstructions.

status_evidence.title: Imaging with Confidence: Uncertainty Quantification for High-dimensional inverse problems
status_evidence.snippet: Confidence regions for complex pixel values are derived from a debiased estimator's Gaussian distribution, yielding magnitude and phase confidence intervals.
status_evidence.claim: Debiased estimators allow construction of pixel-wise magnitude/phase confidence intervals.
